title: Anti-infective drugs that eradicate dormant persisters without seeding genetic resistance

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a clinically tolerated drug or drug combination that eliminates both actively growing bacteria and established dormant persisters, prevents their return after treatment stops, and withstands defined tests for selection of high-level genetic resistance. Persisters are growth-arrested phenotypic variants that survive antibiotic exposure without resistance mutations being required. Their temporary tolerance is distinct from inherited resistance, and surviving persisters can resume growth after the antibiotic is withdrawn.

Synthesis: the breakthrough concerns the combined clinical performance of eradication, tolerability, durable response, and a robust resistance profile. Experimental persister killing already exists, so killing dormant cells in a laboratory assay alone would not establish this innovation. The title's resistance ambition should be understood as avoiding detectable selection under specified conditions, rather than guaranteeing that resistance can never evolve.

significance.text: Antibiotics transformed treatment of bacterial disease, but persisters leave a specific gap: a surviving minority can restart an infection after apparently effective treatment. The supplied review connects persistence with chronic and medical-device-associated infections and describes persisters as a reservoir from which genetically resistant strains can develop over time. Eliminating that reservoir in a relevant infection could prevent relapse attributable to surviving persisters and reduce one opportunity for subsequent resistance development.

Conditional significance: a tolerated regimen that reliably delivered this combination of effects would substantially expand what anti-infective pharmacology can accomplish. Its direct benefit would be durable control or cure of infections in which the persister reservoir is a demonstrated cause of recurrence. Broader improvements in chronic-infection outcomes would still depend on reaching the relevant sites, host factors, and other causes of treatment failure. Persister eradication alone does not establish general clinical cure.

Limits of the impact claim: this capability would not establish activity against every enzymatic or efflux-based resistance mechanism, permanently prevent resistance evolution, or remove the need for vaccines and infection control. Universal inhibition of ABC and SLC transporters is a separate proposal. The supplied evidence does not establish either its feasibility or the detailed claims previously made about transporter functions in mammalian gut, liver, kidney, and brain.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central missing capability is reliable bactericidal activity against already-established growth-arrested persisters at exposures that mammalian tissues can tolerate. Conventional antibiotics commonly act through growth-associated processes that are relatively inactive in dormant cells; describing these processes as wholly inactive would overstate the supplied evidence. A successful regimen must also address actively growing bacteria, whether through one agent or complementary agents.

Delivery is a separate barrier from identifying a lethal mechanism. Candidate compounds must reach persisters in biofilms, host tissues, and intracellular sites at effective concentrations. Selectivity also matters: membrane-directed killing can have limited therapeutic potential if the agent also damages mammalian membranes. This is a conditional toxicity risk, not evidence that every membrane-active compound necessarily harms mammalian membranes. Strategies that inhibit persister formation may also leave an existing persister population intact.

Additional proposed requirement: the regimen must retain useful activity during explicitly defined resistance-selection challenges. The supplied material does not establish a mechanism that guarantees this property, nor does it support a blanket comparison in which growth-targeting antibiotics necessarily fail through single-step selection. Demonstrating a favorable resistance profile must therefore accompany, rather than be inferred from, successful persister killing.

current_state.text: The supplied source is Hashemi, Dhaouadi Khattab, and Ren's mini review, published on October 15, 2025. It reports experimental persister-killing approaches involving membrane-active compounds, pyrazinamide in the context of Mycobacterium tuberculosis persisters, acyldepsipeptide-mediated activation of the ClpP protease, including ADEP4, and antibiotic combinations. These examples demonstrate that persisters are not intrinsically impossible to kill. They do not establish the full proposed combination of clinical tolerability, eradication at infection sites, relapse prevention, and resistance robustness.

The review distinguishes preventing persister formation from killing persisters that have already formed. Its limitations are conditional: formation-inhibiting approaches may not affect established persisters, and effectiveness across species remains a requirement for broader usefulness. It does not demonstrate that several strategies categorically fail across species. Likewise, its membrane-toxicity discussion identifies a possible off-target liability rather than universal failure of direct-killing agents.

No clinical regimen satisfying the complete proposed demonstration is documented in the supplied material. That is a limitation of this evidence set, not proof that no such regimen exists. The supplied review assessment reports complete retained HTML and PDF text without recorded extraction problems, but both represent the same review rather than independent verification of the underlying primary studies. Retrieval on November 1, 2026 does not update the review's October 2025 evidence, and the empty freshness-search record leaves subsequent clinical and experimental developments unresolved.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed convincing demonstration: in a controlled human chronic or device-associated infection study, or a model with demonstrated predictive agreement for that infection, a tolerated regimen eliminates actively growing bacteria and established persisters to prespecified detection limits. The protocol should document exposure at the relevant infection sites and prevent relapse over a prespecified observation period after drug withdrawal. A result in one laboratory strain grown in broth would not establish this clinical capability.
completion_criteria.label: Tolerated regimen eradicates growing bacteria and persisters without relapse

completion_criteria.text: Proposed measurement requirements: distinguish phenotypic persistence from genetic resistance and test whether apparently eliminated cells can resuscitate after treatment. Colony counts alone should not carry the entire eradication claim. Persisters can themselves form colonies after resuscitation, so colony-forming bacteria and persisters should not be treated as mutually exclusive populations. Detection limits, resuscitation conditions, relapse definitions, follow-up duration, and tolerability endpoints should be specified before testing.
completion_criteria.label: Measurements distinguish persistence from resistance and test post-treatment resuscitation

completion_criteria.text: Proposed resistance demonstration: use a defined selection protocol with prespecified thresholds for high-level resistance, an appropriate standard-antibiotic comparator, and measurements of susceptibility before and after exposure. Failure to detect high-level resistance in the candidate regimen would be more convincing if the comparator selected it under the same relevant challenge. Such a result would establish a bounded resistance profile for that protocol; it would not establish permanent immunity to resistance evolution.
completion_criteria.label: Prespecified selection tests detect no high-level resistance after exposure

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: independent replication should reproduce eradication, post-withdrawal durability, tolerability, and resistance findings in the claimed indication. Additional strains, species, biofilm conditions, or infection sites would be necessary to support broader claims. These are proposed criteria rather than established standards, and no numerical thresholds are supplied here. Finite testing would establish demonstrated breadth within the tested conditions, not literal universality.
completion_criteria.label: Independent replication reproduces regimen outcomes within the claimed indication

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: PHA-02, prospective prediction of human efficacy, dose, and major toxicity, overlaps with the need for a model that predicts persister killing and tolerable exposure in people. PHA-02 concerns predictive capability across drug development; PHA-08 concerns an anti-infective treatment capability. A predictive model could help validate PHA-08 without itself supplying an effective regimen.

Roster-based synthesis: PHA-05, systemic pharmacological access to brain parenchyma for arbitrary drug classes, and PHA-11, reliable oral systemic exposure for folded peptides and proteins, share delivery concerns with this concept. Their barriers remain distinct: access to brain tissue and oral absorption do not establish penetration into biofilms, infected tissues, or intracellular persister niches. They could become complementary capabilities for particular agents or infection sites.

Roster-based synthesis: PHA-13, a medicine that holds its own therapeutic window without an external controller, overlaps with maintaining effective exposure while limiting host toxicity. PHA-08 requires an adequate therapeutic window but does not require the medicine to regulate that window autonomously. PHA-01, pharmacological control of proteins lacking usable binding pockets, could contribute target-access strategies, but persister eradication need not depend on solving that broader protein-control problem.

Roster-based synthesis: PHA-03, prevention of idiosyncratic immune-mediated drug injury, and PHA-04, antigen-chosen control of immune memory, concern host immune pharmacology. Neither should be merged with bacterial persistence: immune-mediated toxicity differs from membrane toxicity, and controlling immune memory does not itself establish killing of dormant bacteria. The remaining roster concepts address other therapeutic capabilities and remain separate entries.

change_log.change: Preserved PHA-08's identity and title while defining its resistance ambition through bounded selection tests.
change_log.reason: The evidence supports the persister-control goal but does not establish resistance-proof treatment or permanent prevention of resistance evolution.

change_log.change: Replaced absolute dormant-target inactivity and universal membrane toxicity with reduced target activity and conditional off-target toxicity.
change_log.reason: The reviewed source describes growth-associated processes as relatively inactive and toxicity as a risk when an agent also affects mammalian membranes.

change_log.change: Removed the blanket single-step resistance comparison with growth-targeting antibiotics.
change_log.reason: The supplied evidence does not establish that comparison; resistance robustness remains a separate proposed performance requirement.

change_log.change: Integrated biofilm, tissue, and intracellular delivery barriers with the distinction between preventing persistence and killing established persisters.
change_log.reason: These explain why experimental killing alone does not establish clinically useful eradication.
The review states possible ineffectiveness against formed persisters and a need for cross-species effectiveness, rather than categorical failure.

change_log.change: Bounded clinical-status claims to the supplied October 2025 review and preserved the November 2026 freshness limitation.
change_log.reason: Complete extraction of a review does not constitute independent primary-study verification or a current comprehensive clinical search.

change_log.change: Expanded proposed completion criteria to include resuscitation, detection limits, follow-up, tolerability, resistance thresholds, and replication.
change_log.reason: These make the proposed demonstration interpretable while recognizing that persisters can form colonies and finite tests establish only bounded breadth.

change_log.change: Qualified clinical impact and removed unsupported detailed mammalian ABC/SLC barrier assertions.
change_log.reason: Persister elimination supports prevention of attributable relapse, not universal cure; the supplied source does not substantiate the transporter physiology claims.

change_log.change: Added explicit distinctions with relevant roster entries.
change_log.reason: Shared prediction, delivery, safety, and target-access requirements do not make those innovations interchangeable with persister eradication.

unresolved_issues: Whether developments after the October 2025 review include a regimen meeting the combined goal remains unresolved because no freshness-search evidence was supplied.

The underlying experimental studies were not independently verified in the supplied review; their precise doses, effect sizes, model performance, and resistance-selection results remain unestablished here.

The appropriate indication, predictive model, detection limits, resuscitation procedures, relapse follow-up, tolerability endpoints, and resistance thresholds require specification before the proposed demonstration can be executed.
The achievable breadth across bacterial species, strains, biofilms, tissues, and intracellular sites remains unresolved.
The feasibility and physiological consequences of universal ABC/SLC transporter inhibition require separate evidence and do not resolve this concept's resistance requirement.

brief.title: Medicines that clear infections hiding in dormant bacteria
possible: People whose infections return because dormant bacteria survived treatment could receive medicines that kill these survivors alongside growing bacteria. These survivors, called persisters, temporarily tolerate antibiotics without needing inherited resistance.
Treatment could keep those infections from returning after the medicines stop, at doses patients can tolerate, while passing defined tests for the emergence of strong inherited drug resistance.
why: For patients with persistent infections, including those involving medical devices, eliminating persisters could remove a cause of relapse. It could also remove a reservoir from which genetically resistant bacteria can develop.

sources.who: Mohamad Javad Hashemi, Yousr Dhaouadi Khattab and Dacheng Ren
sources.showed: Their review describes experimental ways to kill persisters, including damaging bacterial membranes and combining drugs. It distinguishes killing existing persisters from preventing their formation.
sources.cited_for: Persisters can be killed through targets that remain vulnerable during dormancy.
sources.not_established: The review does not demonstrate a tolerated treatment that combines eradication, lasting protection from relapse and resistance robustness.

sources.who: B. P. Conlon, K. Lewis and colleagues
sources.showed: The experimental antibiotic ADEP4 combined with rifampicin eradicated Staphylococcus aureus biofilms, bacterial communities inside a protective layer, in laboratory tests and a mouse infection model.
sources.quote: kills persisters by degrading over 400 proteins, forcing cells to self-digest.
sources.cited_for: A drug combination eradicated a persistent bacterial infection in mice.
sources.not_established: Mouse eradication does not establish lasting human benefit or a robust resistance profile; mutants resistant to ADEP4 arose readily.

sources.who: Kuan-Yi Lu, Brian P. Conlon and colleagues
sources.showed: The compound KL1 altered the environment inside host cells, making persisters more vulnerable to antibiotics. It also enhanced antibiotic activity in mouse infection models.
sources.quote: KL1 alone does not promote bacterial outgrowth or show detectable cytotoxicity.
sources.cited_for: Changing the host environment can help antibiotics attack persisters hiding inside cells.
sources.not_established: Enhanced antibiotic killing does not establish complete eradication, prevention of relapse or clinical tolerability.

sources.who: Joseph Fanous, Beatrice Claudi, Dirk Bumann and colleagues
sources.showed: In infected mice and cultures mimicking tissues, nutrient starvation made the wider Salmonella population survive antibiotics. Colony counts misleadingly suggested a distinct persister subset.
sources.quote:
Thus, nutrient access 
controlling replication rate dominated antibiotic survival.
sources.cited_for: Measurements must distinguish a persister subset from widespread bacterial survival.
sources.not_established: This explains poor clearance in the tested Salmonella conditions, rather than demonstrating a persister-eradicating treatment.

shown: Conlon and colleagues eradicated a bacterial biofilm infection in mice using a drug combination. Lu and colleagues also made bacteria hiding inside host cells more vulnerable to antibiotics.
missing: A tolerated treatment must eliminate growing bacteria and established persisters, with no relapse after withdrawal.
Effective drug concentrations must reach protected communities, tissues and the insides of host cells.
Defined exposure tests must find no emergence of high-level inherited resistance.

milestones.label: Tolerated treatment clears bacteria without relapse
milestones.explanation: A controlled human study, or a model proven to predict that infection's outcomes, would have to show eradication without relapse after withdrawal. This would connect persister killing to lasting treatment benefit.

milestones.label: Tests distinguish dormancy, resistance and recovery
milestones.explanation: Measurements would have to distinguish temporary persistence from inherited resistance and test whether survivors can resume growth. This would make an eradication claim credible beyond colony counts alone.

milestones.label: Defined exposure tests find no high-level resistance
milestones.explanation: Prespecified tests would have to compare resistance before and after exposure against a standard antibiotic. This would establish resistance performance within those conditions.

milestones.label: Independent teams reproduce the treatment's combined results
milestones.explanation: Independent teams would have to reproduce eradication, durability, tolerability and resistance findings for the claimed infection. This would establish reproducibility and the boundaries of the claim.

uncertain: Which infections depend enough on persisters for their elimination to prevent relapse?
What detection limits, recovery tests and follow-up periods would convincingly establish eradication?
How broadly would success extend across bacterial species and infection sites, and how long would resistance protection last?

page.title: Antibacterial regimens that eradicate persister cells
page.definition: A drug regimen eliminates growing bacteria and established dormant persisters—temporarily antibiotic-tolerant cells able to resume growth—and produces sustained cure of a defined human infection at tolerated exposures. Acquired genetic resistance remains undetected within specified tests and follow-up.

goal.need: In a 2010 study, late Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from 10 of 14 people with cystic fibrosis produced elevated persister levels; most of these isolates did not have higher antibiotic resistance. These observations motivate targeting antibiotic-tolerant survivors alongside growing bacteria. They do not quantify how much clinical recurrence persister eradication would prevent.

statements.body: Joint Programming Initiative on Antimicrobial Resistance
statements.quote: Anti-Persistance aims to target the mechanisms of pathogenic bacteria that regulate stress and are involved in persistence
statements.context: The initiative's therapeutics pipeline describes the funded Anti-Persistence project's objective.

statements.quote: to penetrate biofilm and eradicate the persister bacteria protected by it.
statements.context: The developer describes its objective for PLG0206 against biofilms, bacterial communities embedded in a protective matrix on medical implants.

completion.title: An approved regimen eradicates persisters in patients and sustains cure without detected acquired resistance.
completion.criterion: For one bacterial indication, a regulator approves a regimen supported by direct evidence that it eliminates growing bacteria and established dormant persisters at the infection site in patients, with sustained cure after treatment withdrawal and no acquired genetic resistance detected in prespecified laboratory and clinical assessments. The studies supply detection limits, recovery assessments, recurrence follow-up, resistance definitions and safety endpoints. All components must be met in the same indication at tolerated exposures; laboratory killing or clinical cure alone does not satisfy this combined test.
completion.set_by: Atlas; no external body located defines this combined clinical and microbiological test.
completion.basis: FDA antibacterial microbiology guidance and drug-review definitions, the 2019 persistence consensus, JPIAMR's pipeline, the 2025 review and PLG0206 trial descriptions were searched for a combined human eradication, relapse and resistance criterion; none was found. This Atlas criterion confines the claim to one licensed indication and the documented tests and follow-up. Approval supplies the benefit–risk decision; direct persister clearance and resistance outcomes require additional evidence.

milestones.title: A drug regimen eliminates established bacterial persisters below the culture-detection limit in vitro.
milestones.criterion: Conlon et al.'s endpoint is clearance of established Staphylococcus aureus persisters below the assay's culture-detection limit. Published on 13 November 2013, ADEP4 met that endpoint; ADEP4 plus rifampicin also cleared biofilms after 72 hours, without regrowth after medium replacement. The accessible killing-assay captions do not specify replicate counts.
milestones.set_by: Conlon et al., published 2013 S. aureus experimental protocol; a study-specific endpoint, not a consensus qualification threshold.
milestones.threshold_quote: eradication of persisters below the limit of detection

milestones.title: A drug regimen clears an established mouse bacterial infection below detection within 24 hours.
milestones.criterion: Clear an established bacterial biofilm infection to the culture-detection limit in the published animal model. Conlon et al. reported this after 24 hours of ADEP4 plus rifampicin in neutropenic mice with S. aureus thigh infection; groups contained 5 mice. The experiment did not establish freedom from relapse after treatment withdrawal.
milestones.set_by: Conlon et al., published 2013 S. aureus mouse-infection protocol; a study-specific endpoint.
milestones.threshold_quote: sterilization of the infected tissue to the limit of detection within 24 hours

milestones.title: A persister-active candidate yields human exposure and safety data sufficient to design phase 2 studies.
milestones.criterion: FDA's phase 1 definition calls for sufficient human pharmacokinetic and pharmacological information to design scientifically valid phase 2 studies. A PLG0206 study published on 18 January 2022 randomized 47 healthy adults: 35 received drug and 12 placebo. No serious treatment-emergent adverse events were reported; two participants stopped drug administration because of moderate infusion reactions. These findings do not establish safety during repeated treatment or in infected patients.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Drug Development and Review Definitions, Phase I Clinical Studies; a general drug-development criterion.
milestones.threshold_quote: permit the design of well-controlled, scientifically valid, Phase 2 studies.

milestones.title: A persister-active regimen reaches infected patients in a phase 1b study.
milestones.criterion: Peptilogics' phase 1b study NCT05137314 administered PLG0206 during surgical debridement with antibiotics and retention of an infected knee prosthesis. Its two cohorts contained 7 patients each. On 19 September 2023, the sponsor reported no treatment-related serious adverse events and no recurrence in 13 of 14 patients through 180 days. These were noncomparative interim results reported in a press release, not peer reviewed.
milestones.set_by: Peptilogics, NCT05137314 phase 1b study design published in its 19 September 2023 announcement; written for knee-prosthesis infection.
milestones.threshold_quote: The trial is an open-label study that consisted of two seven-patient cohorts

milestones.title: A persister-active regimen lowers joint-infection treatment failure at 12 months in a randomized trial.
milestones.criterion: RETAIN, NCT07214311, tests superiority of PLG0206 over placebo irrigation, added to surgical debridement, antibiotics and implant retention for infection after knee replacement. The primary endpoint is treatment failure at 12 months; planned enrollment is approximately 240 patients. Demonstrated superiority on that endpoint meets this milestone. On 5 November 2026, the sponsor announced UK enrollment, not efficacy results; that announcement was not peer reviewed. Public descriptions do not supply the numerical statistical success boundary.
milestones.set_by: Peptilogics, RETAIN phase 2/3 protocol objective described in its 10 March 2026 announcement; written for knee-prosthesis infection.
milestones.threshold_quote: The primary endpoint is treatment failure, assessed 12 months after DAIR.

not_found: No external combined success criterion for human persister eradication, sustained cure, tolerability and absence of detected acquired resistance was located.
ClinicalTrials.gov returned only interface text when the two PLG0206 study pages were opened; clinical targets were available in the sponsor's documents.
Public RETAIN descriptions did not provide the complete treatment-failure definition, numerical statistical success boundary or a no-acquired-resistance endpoint.
No published result satisfying the combined completion test was located.
